frames.title: Explain first
frames.narration: You asked for this: sometimes you just want to know what's going on, in the repo or in a transcript, and then decide whether a plan follows. Today, every video needs a plan first.

frames.title: Today, every video hangs off a plan
frames.narration: Every video today hangs off something: the system video off the whole repo, and the plan video and the walkthrough off a plan. So what does the review server do? What happened in this session? What does this branch change? What changed since Monday? None of these has a video. The agent answers in chat, in text.

frames.title: Earlier plans
frames.narration: Earlier plans lead here. Videos that make sense added fresh eyes, two fresh agents that look at a video before you do, and Ask about this. The plan guide puts the whole plan behind its video. Walkthroughs that help ask a quick check only where there's something to predict. Better visuals put the real thing on screen.

frames.title: What changes
frames.narration: Three changes. Steps one and two: you can ask for an explainer, a video of something that's there, with no plan behind it and nothing to decide. Steps three and four: you review it on the same page, and a plan can follow. Step five: it stays honest, every fact from its sources, and private, a transcript kept out of the repo.

frames.title: Step 1: four kinds
frames.narration: Step one: four kinds of explainer. A part of the repo: the review server is six files and five decisions. A transcript or a log, the record of a session or a run: the session building this repo since last Tuesday is over twenty-one thousand lines. A change: a branch of thirty-three files. A period: since Monday, thirty commits and nineteen decisions. Each runs two to five minutes, and shows the real thing: the code, the lines, the diff.

frames.title: Question 1: the whole source behind it
frames.question: Is an explainer's whole source there to read, behind the video?

options.label: No guide
options.why: The explainer is its video; the rest of the transcript or the diff is not shown.

options.label: Transcripts and changes
options.why: A transcript or a change gets a guide with the whole of it, a click from each moment.

options.label: Every kind
options.why: Every explainer gets a guide, a part's files and a period's commits included.

frames.narration: Question one. That session is over twenty-one thousand lines, and its video quotes a dozen. A: no guide; you get the video. B: a guide for a transcript and a change: the whole transcript, organized, or the full diff, a click from each moment. C: a guide for every kind. I recommend B: the two with far more than a video can hold. Is the whole source there to read?

frames.title: If A: the video only
frames.narration: With A, the session is only the lines its scenes quote.

frames.title: If B: a guide for a transcript and a change
frames.narration: With B, each moment of the session's video opens its turns on the guide.

frames.title: If C: a guide for every kind
frames.narration: With C, a part's guide also holds its files, and a period's its commits.

frames.title: Step 2: ask for one
frames.narration: Step two: you ask in your own words, and the agent runs one command. The explainer gets a folder of its own, and a row of its own on the review page, which says how many commits have landed since.

frames.title: Step 5: honest
frames.narration: Step five: honest. Each scene names where its facts come from, and a new check fails a quoted line its source doesn't hold word for word. Fresh eyes look at it, as at every video. plan.title: Explain first: a video of what is going on, before any plan
plan.problem:
The owner:

> "i do think we have various stages where we want to just know whats going on in the repo, or transcripts
> that result, etc, instead of a video always based on a plan, like i might just ask for a video for
> explaining first then we can decide if we want a plan too"

### What we have

Every video hangs off a plan, or off the whole system:

- **The plan video** is made before the code, from `plan.md`, and asks the plan's questions.
- **The walkthrough video** is made after the code, from `walkthrough.md`, and asks you to accept or flag
  the choices the agent made alone.
- **The system video** explains the whole repo from `spec.md`, `system.json` and `glossary.md`
  (`.reelplanning/system-video/`, 5–8 minutes), kept current after every accepted walkthrough (D-003).

So a question like "what does the review server do?", "what happened in this session?", "what does this
branch change?" or "what changed since Monday?" has no video. Today the agent answers it in chat, in text,
or it becomes a plan before anyone has seen what is there. The pieces a video of it would need already exist:

- `reelplanning build` turns any `STORYBOARD.md` and `SCRIPT.md` into a video, checks it (the terms, the
  frames, the details) and says its length; fresh eyes look at it before you do (D-227).
- The review page plays any built video, with marks, comments and Ask about this (D-226). Its library lists
  the system video and each plan's two videos, one row a plan (D-224).
- `reel record` files a review under a plan's `reviews/`, and adds what you watched and looked up to your
  memory, `~/.reelplanning/you.jsonl` (D-106, D-218).
- The skill already makes a one-off video under `videos/<slug>/` when someone declines to set up
  `.reelplanning/`, but nothing lists it, reviews it or leads anywhere from it.
- The plan guide (approved, not built: D-228, D-229, D-230) puts the whole of a plan behind its video: the
  full diff and the real outputs, a click away from the moment that shows them.

### Real sizes, today

- **A part of the repo:** the review server is six files, 951 lines (`scripts/review.mjs` and five more), with
  five decisions in force on it.
- **A transcript:** the Claude Code session that has been building this repo since 2026-09-22 (the one this
  plan was written in): 21,562 lines, 101 MB of JSONL.
- **A change:** videos-that-make-sense's five build commits (`4dc6bfc` to `cc0dde0`): 33 files, 1,433 lines
  added and 50 removed outside the plan folders.
- **A period:** since Monday (2026-09-28): 30 commits, 19 decisions logged, three plans moved.

steps.title: Four kinds of explainer, and what each shows (question 1)
steps.text:
*Independent.*

An **explainer** is a video that explains something that is there: a part of the repo, a transcript, a
change or a period. It asks no plan questions and changes nothing. It is 2–4 minutes (a transcript up to 5),
one to three chapters, and it shows the real thing wherever it can (D-166): the code at the one or two places
that carry the idea, a real run, the transcript's own lines, the diff, the ledger's rows.

| Kind | You ask | It reads | It shows |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A part** | "explain the review server", "what's going on in this repo" | the part's files (from `system.json`), its `spec.md` section, its glossary rows, the decisions on it | what it is for, one real run through it, where it sits among the parts, what is decided and what is open |
| **A transcript or log** | "what happened in this session", "why did last night's CI run fail" | the session's JSONL (Claude Code keeps it under `~/.claude/projects/`), or a CI log (`gh run view <id> --log`) | what was asked, what was done in order, the turning points (an error, a change of course), the choices the agent made alone, what is left |
| **A change** | "explain this branch", "explain PR 42" | the diff (`git diff`, `gh pr diff`), the commits' messages, the tests that ran | what it changes, as a map of its files, each with one line; then the one or two places that carry the idea; what it chose |
| **A period** | "what changed since Monday" | `git log` over the period, the decision log's rows in it, the reviews filed in it | the plans that moved, the decisions made, what shipped, what is waiting on you |

**Not the system video.** A part explainer is narrower and made when you ask; the system video stays the one
that is kept current (D-003). "What's going on in this repo", asked where the system video is current, opens
the system video; where it is behind, the explainer is of what changed since it was last current (a period). An explainer is a snapshot: it says which commit it explains, and the page says
how many commits have landed since.

**Not the walkthrough.** A change explainer has no plan to compare with, so it has no choices to accept or
flag. A pull request that needs a walkthrough still gets its plan folder (D-200).

Whether an explainer has a guide behind it, the whole transcript or the whole diff a click from its moment,
is question 1. The guide is the plan guide's: its parts open from the video over the paused frame, and the full
page opens from them (D-228, D-246; the plan guide's fifth prototype). A plan's guide is built from `plan.md`
(D-244); an explainer's would be built from its pinned sources. Until the guide is built, an explainer is its
video, with a detail where one scene needs more.

#### Cases

| Case | Example | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| A part | "explain the review server" | reads its six files and five decisions; about 3 minutes; one real run of a review landing in the inbox |
| The whole repo | "what's going on in this repo" | the system video, when it is current; when it is behind, a period explainer of what changed since |
| A transcript | "what happened in this session" | reads the session's JSONL (21,562 lines); up to 5 minutes; its turning points, with their own lines |
| A log | "why did last night's CI run fail" | reads the run's log; about 2 minutes; the failing line, and the commit it ran on |
| A change | "explain this branch" | reads the diff (33 files); about 3 minutes; the map, then the two places that carry it |
| A period | "what changed since Monday" | reads 30 commits and 19 decisions; about 3 minutes; the plans that moved, what waits on you |

#### Interface

```
explain.md      # what you asked, in your words; the kind; what it will cover and leave out
sources.json    # each source pinned: the commit, the paths and their hashes, a transcript's path, hash and lines
STORYBOARD.md   # kind: explainer (front matter); no decision beats; - source: on each scene (step 5)
```

#### Example

You ask "explain the review server". The agent reads its six files, its `spec.md` section, and the five
decisions on it, and makes a three-minute video in two chapters: what the server is for, and one review
going from Send into the inbox and on to a waiting session. It shows `scripts/review.mjs` at the place a
review is handed on, and a real run in a scratch clone.

steps.title: Ask for one: the skill, a command, and a folder of its own
steps.text:
*Needs step 1.*

**You ask in your own words.** The skill's triggers gain "explain …", "what's going on in …", "what happened
in …", "walk me through this branch" and "what changed since …". The agent runs the command, builds the video
as it builds any other (`reelplanning build`, fresh eyes, the page), and opens it. No plan is written.

**The command** gathers and pins the sources, so the video can only say what they say:

```
reelplanning explain part "the review server"
reelplanning explain transcript <file.jsonl | this-session | ci:<run-id>>
reelplanning explain change <branch | commit..commit | pr:<n>>
reelplanning explain since <date>
```

It makes `.reelplanning/explainers/<date>-<slug>/` with `explain.md` (your words, the kind, what it will
cover), `sources.json` (the commit it starts from, each file's path and hash; for a transcript, its path, hash
and line count, never its text) and the video's start (`video/`, its brief with `kind: explainer`). The agent
writes the storyboard from the sources and builds; `build` holds it to 2–4 minutes (5 for a transcript), a
warning past that, as for any video.

**On the review page** an explainer is a row of its own kind, **Explainer**, beside the plans' rows: its
title, its length, "explained at `dee5830`, 12 commits since", and what came of it (Done, or "planned: <the
plan>"). The review server serves it as it serves the plans' videos.

#### Cases

| Case | Example | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Asked in chat | "what changed since Monday?" | the agent runs `reelplanning explain since 2026-09-28` and builds |
| Asked by command | `reelplanning explain change 4dc6bfc~1..cc0dde0` | the folder and its sources; the agent is asked to write the video |
| Opened after the repo moved | the review server explainer, 12 commits later | it plays as it was built; the row says "12 commits since" |
| Asked again | "explain the review server" a week later | a new folder, a new date; the old one stays |

#### Interface

```
reelplanning explain <kind> <what> [--slug <slug>]
  ✓ .reelplanning/explainers/2026-09-29-review-server/ · part · 6 files, 5 decisions, pinned at dee5830
review page row   Explainer · the review server · 3:10 · explained at dee5830, 12 commits since · Done
```

#### Example

"What changed since Monday?" makes `2026-09-29-since-monday/`: 30 commits, 19 decisions, three plans. The
video, three minutes: videos-that-make-sense built and accepted, the plan guide approved, 19 decisions, and
what waits on you (the plan guide's question 1, left unanswered).

steps.title: Review it: the same player, and Finish says what comes next
steps.text:
*Needs step 2.*

**The same player.** You mark, comment, look words up and Ask about this, as on any video. Ask about this
answers from the explainer's sources, the glossary and the scene ("from `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs`, line 56").

**No plan questions.** An explainer asks nothing to decide: `build` fails a `- decision:` scene in a video
of kind `explainer`. A quick check goes where there is something to predict, asked just before the scene
that shows it, as in a walkthrough (D-222): "you press Send twice on the same review: how many runs
start?", then the run shows it. Many explainers have none.

**Finish** has three ends instead of Approve and Request changes:

- **Done**: you know what you wanted to know.
- **Explain more**: your comments and questions come back as the next version: the scenes they are on
  rebuilt, and a scene for each question, with fresh eyes again.
- **Plan this**: a plan starts from what you said (step 4).

**What a review of it produces.** `reel record <explainer-dir>` files it, as every review, under the
explainer's `reviews/`, with a `.md` of your comments by scene and your questions, answered or not. Your
memory gets what you watched and looked up (D-218: a word you know stops being underlined). **Nothing goes
into the decision log**, since only an answer is a decision, and an explainer asks none; a comment like "this
looks wrong" is kept with the review, and goes into a plan if you press Plan this.

#### Cases

| Case | Example | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Done, with comments | two comments on the review server's scene 4 | filed; memory updated; no decision logged |
| Explain more | "why does Send twice start one run?" asked on scene 4 | the next version: scene 4 rebuilt, a scene answering it |
| Plan this | "make a waiting review easy to see" in your own words | filed; step 4 |
| A quick check | "Send pressed twice: how many runs start?" | answered, then the scene runs it; memory counts it |

#### Interface

```
Finish            Done · Explain more · Plan this        (in place of Approve · Request changes)
reviews/explainer-<time>.json   { kind: "explainer", end: "done" | "more" | "plan", comments, questions, ... }
reviews/explainer-<time>.md     ## Comments by scene · ## Questions you asked · ## What you want next
```

#### Example

You watch the review server explainer, ask "why does a second Send not start a second run?" on scene 4, and
press Done. The page answered it from `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs`; the review is filed with the question and its
answer; the decision log does not change.

steps.title: Plan this: a plan that starts from the explainer (question 2)
steps.text:
*Needs step 3.*

**Plan this** files the review, then the agent writes a plan, as it would when asked in chat, with the
explainer as its start:

- `reel new-plan … --from <explainer-dir>` makes the plan folder, and `plan.md` opens with a line naming the
  explainer, "Explained first: `2026-09-29-review-server`".
- **The problem** quotes you: your comments by scene, the questions you asked, and what you wrote under "What
  you want next". The agent writes the steps from there and the check runs as for any plan (`reel check`).
- **The plan video leans on the explainer.** `reel prereqs` puts it first under Before you watch, like any
  video the plan builds on. How much the plan video says again is question 2.

A plan started this way is an ordinary plan from then on: its review, its decisions, its walkthrough. The
explainer's row says "planned: <the plan>", and the plan's row links back to it.

#### Cases

| Case | Example | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Plan this with comments | two comments on scene 4 | both quoted in the plan's problem, with their scene |
| Plan this with a question | "why does Send twice start one run?" answered on the page | the question and its answer quoted |
| A plan video after it | the waiting-reviews plan | Before you watch lists the explainer first |
| Plan this twice | a second plan from the same explainer | a second plan folder; the row lists both |

#### Interface

```
reel new-plan <repo> <slug> --from <explainer-dir>
plan.md         Explained first: `2026-09-29-review-server` (its review: reviews/explainer-<time>.md)
STORYBOARD.md   before: explainer:2026-09-29-review-server | what the review server does, and your two comments
```

#### Example

You press Plan this on the review server explainer, with "make a waiting review easy to see" on scene 4. The
plan `2026-09-30-waiting-reviews` opens with that comment in its problem; its video starts on what changes, and its
Before you watch lists the explainer (3:10) first.

steps.title: Honest and private: facts from their sources, a transcript kept out of git (question 3)
steps.text:
*Needs steps 1 and 2.*

**Facts from the sources, and only them.** Each scene that says a fact names where it comes from, `- source:`
(`scripts/review.mjs:200-230`, `transcript:turns 212-240`, `git:4dc6bfc`, `D-233`). A new check in the build,
`check-sources`, fails a quoted line (inside a `data-artifact`) that its source does not hold word for word,
and a source that is not pinned in `sources.json`; a scene that states a number with no source is a warning,
a failure under `sources_check: strict` (every new explainer carries it).

**Fresh eyes, as for every video** (D-227): the newcomer and the designer, and every finding answered before
the page opens. An explainer of a transcript or a change also gets a **fact check**: a third fresh agent reads
the narration against the sources, never the agent's own account, and lists each sentence they do not
support. It is the code check's reason (D-001): the agent that did the work is the worst judge of its story.

**Private.** A transcript is read where it is and never copied into the repo; `sources.json` keeps its path,
hash and line count. A quoted line that looks like a secret (a key such as `sk-…` or `ghp_…`, a private key, a
`password=`) or holds an email address stops the build until it is cut or masked (`sk-…REDACTED`); a path in
your home is shown as `~/…`. What else goes into git is question 3; with its recommendation, `.gitignore` keeps
an explainer's voice files and render out, as it does a plan's video's (D-213).

#### Cases

| Case | Example | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| A quoted line its source holds | `export function claim(rp, id, by, extra = {})` from `scripts/lib/inbox.mjs` | passes |
| A quoted line changed by hand | the line retyped with a word missing | `check-sources` fails: not in its source |
| A number with no source | "the server retried three times" | a warning; fails under strict |
| A key in a quoted line | `OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-…` in turn 212 | the build stops until it is masked |
| A sentence the sources do not say | "the run was slow because of the network" | the fact check lists it; it is fixed, or kept with a reason |

#### Interface

```
STORYBOARD.md    - source: scripts/lib/inbox.mjs:50-80            (each scene that says a fact)
                 sources_check: strict                             (front matter)
reelplanning check-sources <video-dir>                             (run by build)
  ✗ scene 5 · quoted line not in scripts/lib/inbox.mjs: "claim(rp, id)"
  ✗ scene 7 · a key in a quoted line (transcript:turn 212): mask it
  △ scene 3 · "three times" with no source
reelplanning fresh-eyes <video-dir> --prompt checker               (transcripts and changes)
```

#### Example

The session explainer quotes turn 212, where a command printed an API key. The build stops on it; the agent
masks it (`sk-…REDACTED`) and builds again. The fact check finds "the tests passed first time" in scene 6; the
transcript shows two runs, so the line becomes "the tests passed on the second run".
